reason: Clicks inside an iframe that sits in a closed shadow root, reached through `page.frames()[1]`. The matrix row says Strider has page frames, but `page.frames` is a FrameTree of ids and URLs with no frame to locate or act on, so there is no frame to click into. The iframe is also in a closed shadow root, which Strider's engine can't see (CONCEPTS.md §8)

Clicks an element in a closed shadow root through the handle `page.evaluateHandle('window.__target')` returns, the only way to reach it: Strider's locators don't search closed shadow roots (CONCEPTS.md §8), and `evaluateHandle` makes isolated-world handles only, with no click (method-elementhandle-click, whose notes say raw handle identity isn't preserved)

Clicks an element in nested closed shadow roots through the handle `page.evaluateHandle('window.__target')` returns, the only way to reach it: Strider's locators don't search closed shadow roots (CONCEPTS.md §8), and `evaluateHandle` makes isolated-world handles only, with no click (method-elementhandle-click)
A timed-out action's message names only its operation and phase, not the element covering the target
A locator scoped to a shadow host doesn't search the host's own shadow root
